Hello,
The preauthorisation is automatically released when the payment is successfully captured or cancelled. However, the reversal by the user’s bank can take up to 30 days ( or longer especially for UK banks) and this depends entirely on the bank internal processes. Kindly advise the user to reach out to their bank regarding these charges with the transaction reference details that can be found here:
For Adyen, the reference available as acquirer reference in the payment attempts page.
Payment > Attempts > Authorisation > authorise > search for acquirerreference.
* For PayU, it is the provider transaction ID
Payment > Attempts > Authorisation > authorise > Response > search for provider_raw_transaction_id
* For Yigim, RRN
Payment > Attempts > Authorisation > authorise > Response > search for rrn
* For Fondy, approval code
Payment > Attempts > Authorisation > authorise > Response > search for approval_code
* For Paystack, authorisation reference
Payment > Attempts > Authorisation > Metadata > Authorisation reference

Article 270
(Acts that can be delegated by the Public Prosecutor's Office to criminal police bodies)
1 - The Public Prosecutor's Office may entrust criminal police bodies with the task of carrying out any steps and investigations relating to the enquiry.


Article 2
Direction of the criminal investigation
1 - The competent judicial authority shall direct the investigation at each stage of the proceedings.
2 - The judicial authority shall be assisted in the investigation by the criminal police bodies.
3 - The criminal police bodies, as soon as they become aware of any crime, shall notify the Public Prosecutor's Office as soon as possible, which may not exceed 10 days, without prejudice to the fact that, within the scope of the general order provided for in Article 270(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, they must immediately begin the investigation and, in all cases, carry out the necessary and urgent precautionary acts to secure the means of evidence.
4 - Criminal police bodies shall act in proceedings under the direction and functional dependence of the competent judicial authority, without prejudice to their hierarchical organisation.
5 - Investigations and acts delegated by the judicial authorities shall be carried out by officials designated by the competent criminal police authorities for this purpose, within the scope of the technical and tactical autonomy necessary for the effective exercise of these duties.
6 - Technical autonomy is based on the use of a set of appropriate knowledge and methods of action, and tactical autonomy consists of choosing the appropriate time, place and manner to carry out the acts corresponding to the exercise of the legal powers of criminal police bodies.
7 - The criminal police bodies shall instigate and carry out the legally admissible steps themselves, without prejudice to the judicial authority being able, at any time, to take over the process, monitor its progress and legality and give specific instructions on the performance of any acts.

IV - It is the responsibility of the Attorney General to issue the general directives and instructions that are necessary to ensure the effective fulfilment by the Public Prosecution Service of the duties inherent to its legal competences.

# In cases relating to events that occurred before 1 March 2008, the information referred to in Article 281(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure must be obtained:

Hi!

The Police in Romania are not yet used to setting limits when it comes to data protection. Probably due to the lack of training at the level of institutions in terms of data protection legislation, they have the wrong impression that being a public authority, they can request absolutely anything.

I understand that it’s a case of theft. The fact that they ask for all the orders from a certain address, without any connection with the address where the theft occurred and without even giving us more selection criteria and what exactly they are looking for, seems too much.

After all, our platform is not the one under investigation, we are not here to give data left or right, we help the investigation, but they must understand that:
- we have some limits regarding customer data, we cannot share without relevant explanations;
- that they must provide us with more information to know what we are looking for exactly;
- and it’s possible that what they ask for, we will not be able to search, for technical reasons.

We should be friendly with them, tell that we are trying to find a solution, but we have the above limitations, and we need their understanding and their support.

Sorina

Hi [~accountid:712020:72878559-0ddb-4588-9bac-a118e3564f70] 

Today I go on annual leave (25/12-2/1 (incl)), so I’m adding some input proactively here just in case you decide the decision is correctly sent to us and you need something to work from in the meantime.

*Regarding legal basis § 205*

* The decision seems to be issued by the police alone, so it’s unclear to me why they have referred to §205. This provision mainly regulates who has authority to decide on seizures, with the main rule that only +the prosecutor+ can decide on seizure of things +that the owner does not want to hand over voluntarily+. Maybe I’m missing some background?
* §205 second paragraph also states that “if the police want to take documents to court for a decision on whether they can be seized, the documents must be sealed in an envelope in the presence of a representative of the [document] owner”. Is the information listed in the decision available only in digital form, or also physical form?

Seizure _can_ be decided by the police alone under the relevant law, (e.g. if there is a risk that the evidence will be destroyed if the seizure is delayed or in connection with a house search), but under other provisions. To assess their applicability I would need some more information:

* The circumstances around how this decision was issued to us, including when and how we received it
* Confirmation that it is a +Rider+ that is suspected of crime (not Bolt)
* Copies of _any_ other correspondence or information in relation to this matter (please note that the +only+ information I have access to regarding what has happened is the information in the decision)

Even if the Police have the right to seize the information, it should be noted that there are exceptions when we’re not obliged to provide seized information anyway. The only relevant to us would in that case be the exception for trade secrets. Given the nature of the information that is being seized I don’t see it would be regarded as trade secrets (but Legal can’t really make that decision - so if you want to check whether the information is commercially sensitive to release, I recommend asking SE RH Local team to confirm). 

Please find translations of the relevant provisions in [+this document+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tru5j8Q9VOEFU8VQgfrGKH4bwpZde77O67MJkDPadBQ/edit].

# Checking results vs CausalPy
CausalPy is an already existing tool that already does the Interrupted Time series analysis, so we might as well use the package instead of custom solution*.

Here it was interesting to compare CausalPy to the models to make sure our methodology understandings match.

This was particularly fruitful, because comparing self-made models to CausalPy highlighted the question of priors for uncertainty intervals (sigma).

Here we just checked that models gave close predictions and uncertainty intervals (not necessarily equal ones).

*One might ask, why we're not going to use CausalPy straight ahead and invent our own solution. We might as well use CausalPy. But as always it's the question of flexibility (custom models) vs ready-to-use solution (causalpy). 

# Checking results vs OLS (without confidence/predictions intervals)

Also it was interesting to compare, how often the predictions would match to a regular OLS solution, because OLS is the best tool to represent our assumptions (just minimizes the MSE with predictors without any priors).

We did not check what confidence/prediction intervals could be, because we understand this is a completely different interpretation

In particular, every driver needs to hold a driving license for at least 3 years, a certificate of TVDE driver issued by the national authority, a course certificate to become a TVDE driver issued by a third party and no criminal record. 

In compliance with the current legislation, Bolt requires these documents for all drivers in the platform, which are verified at the moment a driver account is activated and later on at the time of expiry{color:#ff991f}/renewal {color}of such documents.

Due to privacy related principles, we are unfortunately not able to share this personal data with passengers and make available the documentation for each driver.

* *Control of cars so that there is no extra hours (there are stories of two or three drivers driving one car so that the car is not idle, but only one driver is registered in the system)*

The profession of TVDE drivers is regulated in Portugal. Consequently, only drivers with an account in the platform and fulfilling the legal requirements are able to legally provide transportation services. 

In addition to the documentation compliance in place, we have recently introduced an identity verification {color:#ff991f}tool{color} {color:#ff991f}to ensure only registered drivers provide transportation services through our platform{color}. This means that drivers in the {color:#ff991f}Bolt{color} platform {color:#ff991f}are required{color} to submit a real-time selfie as part of our identity verification process {color:#ff991f}not only as part of the{color} registration {color:#ff991f}process {color}but also {color:#ff991f}-, as well as-{color} later on {color:#ff991f}-and- {color}on a regular basis.

Passengers are also important partners in maintaining the safety of the platform. We recommend each passenger to check that the driver’s face, car make and registration plate match those shown in the app. When in doubt passengers {color:#ff991f}can {color}send us reports that prompt us to to double check the concerns raised.

* *Audio or video monitoring in the car during trips, for the safety of both passenger and driver*

Even though we are committed with the highest safety standard, we must ensure any such measures are implemented in accordance with local regulations. {color:#ff991f}-Even though- {color}Many markets {color:#ff991f}do {color}not enable electronic platforms to implement {color:#ff991f}audio or video monitoring{color} features, {color:#ff991f}however {color}we have recently introduced a safety feature that allow passengers to share trip details. This allows passengers to send the car's make, model, registration number, and live location to friends or family via a shareable link.

* *Instruction to drivers on what they can and cannot do*

Following local regulations, TVDE drivers in electronic platforms work at the service of certified TVDE operators in Portugal. These TVDE operators are independent companies from Bolt and the drivers at their service therefore autonomous from Bolt. 

Nevertheless, the profession of TVDE driver is regulated in Portugal and therefore TVDE operators and their drivers compelled to provide their services in compliance with legislation in place.

Hi [~accountid:5fbb68f578f0180076139818] In this case, we shared *third party courier’s data* with the authority, therefore we do not we have to inform the fleet about this. 

We could inform the couriers, but we usually do not do so as we state this in our Privacy Policy. 

The issue as well is that Jobsplus Agency might be carrying out an investigation and the disclosure could interfere with this investigation.

*When responding to Jobsplus, we could ask them whether Bolt can disclose this matter to the third part couriers or whether this will disrupt a potential investigation.*

If we share *fleet’s information* with the authority (e.g. info about the fleet legal entity etc), this is not personal data of a person but rather of a company - so generally speaking we can inform the Fleet accordingly - unless we suspect that the investigation is sensitive (for example an AML issue), then we should refrain from informing the fleet.

Please note that because of the DSA coming into force in earyl feb, we’ll have to update the Bolt Food T&Cs, and we’ll add at the same time a provision making it clear that Bolt might have to respond to authorities requests without necessarily informing fleets - see below the propose wording for the new T&Cs:

_Confidential Information of the other party may be disclosed to third parties only subject to a prior written notice of the other party or in case required under law, rule or regulation. Furthermore, Bolt may also disclose Confidential Information pursuant to a valid order or request issued by a court, government agency, or regulatory body._

Hope this clarifies the topic and therefore closing this ticket - but pls LMK if you have any follow-up questions. Thanks

# There’s been an experiment in Kenya [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MARTECH-5773|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MARTECH-5773|smart-link] where the model failed to find a proper relation between Android and iOS and as a result produced the predictions that make no sense. I think the reason for this is that Causal Impact is a complicated tool (with so many parameters), so it failed to understand the relation between Android and iOS. So a simpler model (which uses less parameters) could work better.
# It might as well be that Causal Impact complexity leads to more uncertainty (about the model parameters and as a result about the predictions). This could be another argument towards a simpler model
# Causal Impact complexity also leads to some processual drawbacks. Since it’s learning too long (while there’s still some manual work to be done with them), it is very daunting to run the experiments (you always have to check how they work).

ivan.edrennikov: You would not need to create new order page, you can use your current order page, and to this page you would do the redirect. So, how it would work (and how it works for Delivery and Ride Hailing).

1. On _our_ Admin Panel page we would have a list of bookings with URLs like this: `https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/scooter-order/orders?source_id=111111&city_id=222222&user_id=33333`
2.  On _your_ side you would have GET endpoint `scooter-order/orders` for Admin Panel which would accept those parameters.
3. By calling this endpoint you would go to you backend to calculate shard_id from city_id.
4. Then once you know shard_id you would build a new URL, like this: `https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-micromobility/orders/edit/germany/108250509?tab=details` and redirect to it.
So, no need to build special order page, just an endpoint which would do the redirect to existing order page.

For reporting on amounts we have 2 options, we can either report on the *Transaction Currency* or the *Translated Currency*. So for example if we run a Trial Balance report, for say ES001, the amounts under the _transaction currency_ would be in the original amounts the entries were made in, and summed up at the end (this sum would not be correct as different currencies would be summed up to each other, for e.g. GBP 500 + EUR 300 and sum would be 700) and hence we usually have a field for _translated amounts_ which translates all the original amounts into a single currency and then sums up to show correct values.

as of 1 Jan 2024:

* energy drinks must not be sold to minors. 
* energy drink (a beverage with added caffeine or taurine) is a product in the form of a beverage, being a foodstuff (included in the Polish Classification of Goods and Services in Class 10.89 and in Chapter 11), which contains *caffeine in a proportion in excess of 150 mg/l or taurine*, excluding substances occurring naturally in it.
* the producer or importer of energy druink mark the unit packaging of the product visibly, legibly and indelibly and indelibly with the words "Energy drink" or "Energy drink” („Napój energetyzujący” or „Napój energetyczny”)
* there are no specific restrictions on advertising or promotion.

In order to comply with the new regulations, we should implement age verification of users who want to buy energy drinks. Hi [~accountid:61dc710ff63ac80070c15c9d] reverting to this topic:

Indeed, under Polish law only the sales of the alcoholic products is restricted. Alcoholic beverage is understood as beverage containing ethyl alcohol of agricultural origin in an alcoholic strength exceeding 0.5% by volume. Therefore, formally, the beers containing below 0.5% can be sold via platform. 

However:

* there is a [clear recommendation from PAPRA|http://parpa.pl/index.php/aktualnosci/1178-stanowisko-parpa-ws-sprzedazy-piwa-bezalkoholowego] (State Agency for Solving Alcohol Problems) that both sales and promotion of non-alcoholic products should not be targeted at minors (as this shapes drinking habits);
* there are industry self-regulation with respect to non-alcohol beverages [example|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C024SRQA2G6/p1693324068748869?thread_ts=1691495023.565269&cid=C024SRQA2G6]
* the pure use of the word related to alcohol (such as ‘beer’) and in addition - linking this to an alcoholic beverages producer (e.g. Calsberg) - can be understood as an indirect form of alcoholic alcohol advertising (which cannot be targeted at minors either).

Therefore, ideally:

* (i) alcohol / non-alcohol items should be accessible only to adult users - separate tab or these items are blurred in the menu (age verification),
* (ii) the alcohol/non-alcohol beverages should only be distributed/sold to adult users (age verification).
* (iii) the advertisement/ promotion of the non-alcohol/alcohol beverages should pop up in the alcohol tab in the app (after age verification),
* (iv) there are age / health disclaimers on the advertising banners.

Please reach out to [~accountid:5cd9daa0bc70090d6ce26227] as the Bolt Market team is working on enabling 3P alcohol sales through the platform and is working with the product team on the required product solutions (age verification).

* both tobacco and alcohol products can be sold online in CZ, subject to the comms/display obligations, mainly the obligation the seller to inform the customer of the ban on the sale of alcohol and tobacco-related goods to persons under 18 years of age, in clearly visible text, in the case of an e-shop, before clicking on the "Order" button.

Dear Sunny Singh Sapra, 



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *2/12/2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We share a copy of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order data on 2023-10-10, approximate local time of 15:00 [Exported time: UTC. Current local summer time: UTC+1]*

*As it also relates to third party subjects, passengers, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice (fine) received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty notice.*

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link] which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Dear XXX, 
Thank you for the clarification.

We understand national security concerns; however, we believe that the exclusion of all individuals with Russian and Belarusian citizenship is disproportionate to the legitimate aim sought, as only a minor portion of these individuals could potentially pose a national threat. Others are being discriminated against without valid reason or justification.

Furthermore, it is important to note that at the governmental level, a security filter has already been implemented to limit individuals who could pose a national threat from legally staying in Lithuania. Specifically, all drivers in Lithuania are required to obtain an individual activity certificate. To acquire this certificate, third-country nationals of non-EU Member States are required to possess a temporary or permanent residence permit in Lithuania. Obtaining a residence permit involves a thorough verification process by the State Security Department of Lithuania. Consequently, individuals who pose a threat to national security are not permitted to legally reside in Lithuania and provide any services.

Furthermore, drivers on the Bolt platform and app have access to minimal data about passengers. While drivers can view a passenger's name and phone number, the actual phone number is concealed and replaced with a random set of numbers visible to drivers. Drivers are unaware of whether a passenger is an employee of a specific company, a local resident, or a tourist heading to the airport. Additionally, drivers are randomly assigned by the system for each new order, significantly reducing the likelihood of a driver having repeated trips with the same passenger. The Bolt app incorporates safety monitoring during trips, with the system detecting anomalies, such as an unauthorized stop, and initiating communication with both drivers and riders for assistance. If a passenger requests assistance or fails to respond within 3 minutes, Bolt Customer Support is promptly notified.

In light of these measures, we believe that a high level of safety is already ensured, and no additional exclusion of Russian and Belarusian citizens is necessary. Additionally, please note that ride-hailing services in Lithuania are exclusively provided by self-employed drivers. As a result, no contractual relations can exist between Bolt and legal entities with Russian or Belarusian connections. 

Based on the above and considering that the introduction of such a clause is contradictory to the law and with a high probability will trigger scrutiny of Bolt's contractual commitments by the Equal Opportunity Ombudsman and the Lithuanian Competition Council, we kindly urge you to exclude clause 1.2.6 from the technical specification.

* LT law prohibits any advertisement of alcoholic beverages. Any dissemination of information that may lead to alcohol purchase is considered prohibited advertising, e.g. sales campaigns, display of individual shelves, additional/brighter lighting and not possible. 
* The display of discounted prices and the inclusion of alcohol in various promotions is also considered advertising and is prohibited. The price of the drink may be reduced, but the price label cannot show the reduction and only the single lower price may be displayed.
* Also, it is prohibited to use means of distinguishing alcoholic beverages, such as price labels for alcohol, slogans, signs such as "For your bar", "Taste of the day", or "Recommended", as this draws attention to specific alcohol.
* It is not allowed to use such signs and slogans as "elegant", "delicate", "unique" etc.

*ALLOWED* (use can use this info to generate new marketing ideas):

* to add objective info about the taste of alcohol (e.g. "sour", "tangy", "sweet", "bitter", "cherry", etc. flavour that are recognised by taste receptors) in the menus of retail outlets and catering outlets.
* to provide info about the history, production method/technology and awards won by alcoholic beverages on the websites of outlets or companies that produce and sell alcohol
* to include alcoholic cocktail recipes, images of beverages in glasses, objective food pairing recommendations (e.g. "recommended for fish dishes", "suitable for meat dishes", etc.) on the websites of companies producing or selling alcohol, or on sales outlets and menus of catering outlets.

The template should not be changed. Is about the personal info of the employees. Just as info: “

* *You must fill in form 145 when you start workin*g for a company *or when there is a change in your personal or family circumstances* that you had previously reported and at the beginning of each tax year.
* However, many companies will ask their employees to fill in the form at the end of the year to identify any changes that may involve a difference in the IRPF withholding applied to their salary.

h2. Notification of a change of data

* You can file a new form *if your personal and family circumstances change*, for example, the birth of a child. 
* The changes will take effect from the date of the communication, provided that there are at least *five days before the next payroll date*.
* The *new IRPF withholding percentage will be applied to your next paycheck* after the change. 
* If the change supposes the application of a higher withholding percentage,  *you must notify your employer within ten calendar days from the change date*.

h2. What happens if I do not submit form 145 (Legal issues)? 

* If you prefer not to let your company know about any of the circumstances requested in Form 145, *the percentage of IRPF withholding applied by your company may be higher* than the one that corresponds to you.
* It constitutes a *tax infraction to include false, incomplete, or inaccurate* data in form 145 or the non-communication of changes in your personal or family circumstances. You are responsible and not your company, who is only obliged to calculate the withholding percentage based on the information you provide. 
* *Infractions are punishable by a fine* between 35% and 150% of the amounts not withheld for this reason.”

Hi [~accountid:6080743e2ad11c0072b3207c] as discussed, the alignement with the competitors' platforms pricing (wide parity clauses) cannot be added to our contracts due to the competition law concerns:

* under new EU legislation, wide parity clauses are excluded from 30% safe-harbour (cc: [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] Article 5.1(d) [Vertical Block Exemption Regulation|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/PL/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32022R0720#d1e586-4-1] ), same in [PL Regulation|https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WDU20230001033/O/D20231033.pdf] para. 12.4 (the legislator in PL has gone even further and stipulated that such clauses constitute an infringement of competition law) - this means that there is no longer presumption that they are safe as long as the company has a market share below 30%;
* in the past, PL competition office (UOKiK) questioned wide clauses in hotel online booking sector (Hotel Reservation Service, Expedia Lodging Partner, booking.com)[https://uokik.gov.pl/news.php?news_id=11995|https://uokik.gov.pl/news.php?news_id=11995|smart-link] 
* I couldn't find Wolt Restaurants T&C, but from the press articles from other countries, I see that they use narrow parity clauses (same as we do):
** [https://yle.fi/a/3-12223050|https://yle.fi/a/3-12223050|smart-link] 
** [https://www.helsinkitimes.fi/finland/finland-news/domestic/20563-mara-asks-competition-authority-to-look-into-pricing-terms-of-wolt.html|https://www.helsinkitimes.fi/finland/finland-news/domestic/20563-mara-asks-competition-authority-to-look-into-pricing-terms-of-wolt.html|smart-link] 
* Our competitors - e.g. pyszne.pl, have only “Same Price Guarantee“ with respect to the restaurants own online channels (accepted e.g. [in Germany for Lieferando|https://www.bundeskartellamt.de/SharedDocs/Meldung/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2023/12_07_2023_Lieferando.html?nn=3591568], [German pyszne.pl|http://takeaway-restaurant-portal.s3.amazonaws.com/partnersTerms/de/TC_Restaurants_DE_DE.pdf] )

* An HMRC spokesperson said: "We are disappointed with the ruling and are carefully considering the tribunal's decision. Our view remains that the Tour Operators Margin Scheme does not apply to mini-cab businesses."
* The decision also raises the prospect of Uber being victorious in its similar battle with HMRC, which Uber's financial results from August state is worth around 386 million pounds ($490 million). The hearing of Uber's case is likely to take place in 2024. Uber declined to comment on last week's ruling in Bolt's case.

# _1a - So we stop setting any cash aside, but we don't get back the money we have already put by (and is locked up) which could go to the interest?_

(1) Correct - we don't get the money back immediately. We have to apply to HMRC for the return and if they decide to appeal the Judgment they will also apply for a "protective order" to ringfence that money until; (i) we ultimately win; (ii) they win and entitled to keep it. No interest is incurred on the amount held by HMRC (confirming with Deloitte).(2) Procedurally they have 30 days to appeal to the First Tier Tribunal (the same tribunal). If this is rejected (likely), they can apply to the Higher Tax Tribunal which could be 30 to 56 days (confirming with Deloitte) but we believe we should have at least 60 days before an appeal may be granted (assuming that the FTT appeal application is rejected).(3) The Judgment is specific to Bolt so we can absolutely rely on it when it becomes public. However, it becomes a precedent on disclosure for all other operators to rely on the outcome. They will need to seek their own legal advice (usually KCs) to determine if their circumstances fit the same fact pattern. They will no doubt go and get the advice to demonstrate that they took reasonable care and diligence in following what was set at the FTT to apply to their own businesses. Lets say Wheely takes the advice, they will need to create a TOMS model similar to our and will need a KC to say "yes" you substantially look like Bolt and therefore can reasonably expect to rely on the Judgment until appeal.(4) Some modelling needs to be done by the business to determine the best commercial outcome - variables include:

(d) Agency (Rest of UK) - 5% VAT on commission + Principal (London)  - 5% VAT on the full fareThe question is that only a few operators use the TOMS model (Uber, FreeNow and Bolt) - if we utilise TOMS on the Principal Model and take the 5% new rate... *Overview* 

Both Spirable and Hunch offer robust solutions for advertisers aiming to create visually compelling, branded ads at scale. However, their core functionalities cater to slightly different needs.

Hunch primarily excels in DPA. It enables seamless connection to product feeds and utilizes AI-powered tools to craft enhanced, product-focused visuals. This capability makes Hunch particularly advantageous for campaigns where the main goal is to leverage existing product feeds efficiently. If the campaign's focus is on showcasing a dynamic inventory with real-time updates, Hunch stands out as the more suitable choice.

Spirable, on the other hand, doesn't specialize in DPAs to the same extent. While it's possible to create product-focused campaigns, it requires more engineering effort, and the process is generally slower (with a standard SLA of 15 working days). This makes Spirable less ideal for e-commerce centric clients or campaigns where rapid, product-based ad customization is crucial.

*Best practises* 

In terms of campaign execution strategies, both platforms benefit greatly from early personalization, especially in video creatives. Incorporating dynamic elements like location, weather etc, in the first few seconds of the ad can significantly increase engagement. However, it's advisable to avoid overly specific conditions (like precise weather states or exact hours) as this can limit ad delivery. Instead, broader categories such as “Morning/ Afternoon/ Evening” for time, or “Weekday/ Weekend” for days, ensure better coverage and effectiveness.

Location-based ads: when targeting specific locations, it's beneficial to keep the audience broad. Using different variations of a city name or adding a radius to lat-long coordinates can optimize reach while maintaining relevance.

In summary, choose Hunch for dynamic, product feed-driven campaigns, and opt for Spirable when product ads are not the primary focus. Each platform requires a similar level of input and can yield comparable results, but their interfaces and specific functionalities do differ. 

*Examples:* 

* For “sunny ad” *use* weather conditions: _clear sky or few clouds or scattered clouds and temperature_ (optional). *Do not use* only one condition, “sunny ad” = _clear sky_
* Time of day - *use* Morning / Afternoon / Evening or Day / Night. *Do not use* 12-13, 17-19 etc, will not deliver
* Day of week ads - *use* Weekday / Weekend or Mon - Wed / Thur - Sun etc. *Do not use* only one weekday.

Hello everyone,

The response to the lawsuit has been submitted earlier this morning. Please find attached the receipt of the submission for our internal records.

[^ACUSE_RECIBO_ESCRITO_202917.pdf]

For a better understanding, you will find below a summary of the lawsuit and a summary of our response:

+*Summary of the Plaintiff’s claim:*+

* The Plaintiff is engaged in the retail trade of perfumery, clothing and accessories. 
* In order to carry on her business, the Plaintiff purchases goods mainly from two wholesalers: A-DE-TE and Noufabra SA.
* On Wednesday, September 27, 2023, the Plaintiff ordered several units of clothing from both wholesalers via phone. The Plaintiff proposed that both orders be shipped to A-DE-TE's premises and, once there, to have a VTC vehicle pick up the goods and deliver them to the Plaintiff's premises where the Plaintiff would pay the price of the trip. 
* Following the Plaintiff’s proposal, one of A-DE-TE's employees ordered a trip through the Bolt app in order to transport the goods to the Plaintiff's premises, choosing the cash payment option.
* The goods were collected from the premises of A-DE-TE on 27 September 2023 at 13:20 hours by a driver named Jaime, an employee of the company IMOBILITY SL (company fleet registered in the Bolt App), who was driving a Suzuki Suif vehicle with registration number 1154-LLS.
* Due to the driver's tardiness in delivering the goods, the person who ordered the trip tried to contact him several times via the Bolt App, but he never answered the calls.
* The Plaintiff claims from Bolt and IMOBILITY SL the amount of €535.82 (the price of the undelivered goods plus the estimated losses for the time lost in going to court to file the lawsuit).



+*Bolt's arguments to oppose the claim:*+

+Formal arguments+

* *Lack of standing to be sued -* The lawsuit is addressed to Boltest Txfy SL (*“Bolt Spain”*). However, Bolt Spain does not have passive standing in accordance with the provisions of art. 10 of the LEC as it is not the owner of the legal relationship or the object of the litigation attributed to it. Indeed, Bolt Spain is a Spanish company that provides administrative and support services to Bolt Operations OÜ (*“Bolt Estonia*) and the Bolt group, but is not the owner of the Bolt App and does not have any contractual relationship with the passengers and the transportation service providers. For the use of the Bolt App, passengers and transportation service providers contract with Bolt Estonia by accepting the terms and conditions of the latter entity. It is therefore our understanding that, in any event, claims relating to the Bolt App should be addressed to Bolt Estonia  and not to Bolt Spain. We therefore request that the action be dismissed for lack of standing to be sued.
* *Lack of standing to sue -* The Plaintiff, on the other hand, was not the one who requested the transportation service via the Bolt App, but Ms Patricia Martín (an employee of the wholesaler's company  A-DE-TE). Even if the goods allegedly stolen belonged to the Plaintiff, the Plaintiff has no contractual relationship with Bolt Spain, Bolt Estonia or the transportation service provider, and therefore we understand that she lacks standing to sue any of the above for damages or losses suffered in the provision of a service that was not contracted by the Plaintiff.
* *Lack of jurisdiction and competence -*  We understand that the Civil Court lacks jurisdiction and competence to hear the present case given that the facts described by the Plaintiff are subsumable under the criminal type of misappropriation of Article 253 of the Criminal Code:
*# _Those who, to the detriment of another, appropriate for themselves or for a third party, money, effects, securities or any other movable thing, which they have received in deposit, commission or custody, or which have been entrusted to them by virtue of any other title which produces the obligation to hand them over or return them, or who deny having received them, shall be punished with the penalties of Article 248 or, where appropriate, Article 250, unless they are already punished with a more serious penalty in another provision of this Code._
*# _If the amount of the appropriated funds does not exceed 400 euros, a fine of one to three months shall be imposed._
* Indeed, according to the facts of the lawsuit, the driver received the goods from Ms Martin with the obligation to deliver the goods to the Plaintiff at the point of destination indicated by Ms Martin, but on arrival at the point of destination, the driver did not deliver the goods but took them for himself.
Therefore, the Plaintiff should have filed a complaint against the driver for misappropriation of the goods and not brought a civil action against Bolt Spain.

+Substantive arguments+

* According to the facts of the lawsuit, Ms Patricia Martin requested a transportation service through the Bolt App for the transportation of goods purchased by the Plaintiff and not for the transportation of any passengers, whereas, according to the terms and conditions of the Bolt App, the only transportation service that can be provided through the Bolt App is for the carriage of passengers and in no case for the carriage of goods. 
In other words, the users or passengers and the transport service providers, by accepting the terms and conditions of the Bolt App accept that the transportation service provided through the Bolt App is to be for the transportation of passengers and not for the transportation of goods. We consider, therefore, that the user Ms Patricia Martín and the driver in question misused  the Bolt App since the former contracted and the latter provided a goods transportation service in breach of the terms and conditions applicable to them.
* Pursuant to our terms and conditions, Bolt Estonia: (i) does not directly provide the transportation service which is provided by the transportation service provider and (ii) does not assume any responsibility for the performance of the contract for the provision of transportation services between the transportation service provider and the user. Therefore, any claim related to the provision of the transportation service or occurrences in connection with the provision of such service must be addressed to the transportation service provider, who is the actual provider of the service and who, by virtue of the terms and conditions referred to above, is liable to the users for the provision of such service.
* In accordance with our terms and conditions - accepted by the user Ms. Patricia Martin prior to the provision of the service - Bolt Estonia is exempt from any liability for the quality of the service and for any damage or loss that the user may experience as a result of the transportation service provided, and such liability shall be borne by the transportation service provider who actually provides the service.
Furthermore, the judgement of the Supreme Court, Third Chamber, no. 1818/2020, of 30 June 2008.
1818/2020, of 30 December confirms that the information society service providers are exempt from liability for the underlying service that is provided through them.
In view of the above, there would be no basis for a civil claim against Bolt Estonia, Bolt Spain or the Bolt group.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

So the invoice is correct

sql

{noformat}select date(vehicle_last_state_transition_timestamp),count(distinct vehicle_id)
from (
select
  distinct vehicle_id as vehicle_id,
  last_value (created) over (partition by vehicle_id
order by
  created rows between unbounded preceding and unbounded following) as vehicle_last_state_transition_timestamp,
  last_value (to_state) over (partition by vehicle_id
order by
  created,id rows between unbounded preceding and unbounded following) as vehicle_last_state
from
  glue.ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event
where
  to_state in ('sold', 'being_serviced', 'disassembled', 'operational','on_hold', 'being_deployed', 'lost', 'lost_forever', 'collected', 'waiting_for_service', 'waiting_for_deployment', 'dead')
  )
  where vehicle_last_state = 'lost_forever'
  group by 1
  order by 1 desc {noformat}

Not that I am a disbeliever of this, but three things strike me about this transcript:

# They mention at the start of the call, they are calling about a colleague and then later mention that the person is their client. Based on my dealing with the journalists this is not something they would say. - They would normally say ‘Source’ not the client.
# All journalists I have met/spoken to before, have an online presence of some form. But ‘Nicola Walker’ and her phone number show nothing online. Also in the UK, there is a register of Journalist interest for the UK Parliament. Nicola Walker is not on this either. There is no mention of her on the Daily Mail website, company LinkedIn page or Twitter. 
# As per point 2. most journalists have an online presence, but all journalists (unless this is their very, very first report) should have previous work/articles they have done. Again, I can see nothing for a Nicola Walker. 

Whilst it is not an offence to ‘pretend’ to be a journalist. It is an offence to gain access to information or locations under false pretences. It can lead to charges such as fraud or trespassing.

Hi [~accountid:632d88e0748d1bfcb858128d], 

Please check with them one more time and inform them that we *can’t accept* their template as it lacks several necessary clauses. As Bolt is a disclosing party, it is in our interest to protect our information and their template is simply insufficient: 

* Unclear and insufficient definition of confidential information 
* Doesn’t include any exclusions to confidential information 
* No clause Mandatory law disclosures 
* No clause on Scope, Term, termination 
* No Governing law clause
* No Notices clause etc. 

If they still maintain that we need to use their template then you need to inform them that we will have to include additional clauses as per the above so in essence we will have to push to achieve a situation as with our own template. *We can’t accept their template as it is.* 

Please inform them that in order to proceed with these important disclosures, we need to request that they sign our standard mutual NDA. Unlike many other NDAs, the Bolt standard NDA is written on only two pages with the intention of having broad provisions to capture any confidential disclosure or discussion between both parties. It is well balanced to ensure both parties are protected for the mutual disclosures that are made. 

Since their template provides less protection of their and our confidential information I do not see why they can’t agree to use our template as a basis. We do not include any warranties, monetary penalties or similar. If there are any specific clauses they are concerned about in our template then they should inform us and we can discuss if they can be adjusted. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hi, [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35]! I have completed the review of the latest version of the agreement available [*here*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17KS0VmgR3uoZPXwNfZNpmGgGTOEpCSTa/edit]. I have added small changes to the draft directly, but some issues require your prior guidance. Here are the open questions and issues that I have identified: 

* clause 4.1 (ii) - copy of ID document - Telepass states that uploading driving licence by customers is a mandatory requirement, whereas valid ID document is not.
* clause 4.2.8 - Bolt shall hold Telepass harmless in case of a claim regarding use of Bolt Rental - seems reasonable to keep this wording. However, section 5 about liability has no clause that would attribute any liability to Telepass in case of claims related to faults of payment system. Telepass assumes liability for the operation of its IT system, but perhaps we should add provisions that would regulate liability of Telepass as a payment service provider? I think this is needed because payment service entails a bit more than just IT solution, for example, relevant licences or cooperation with a financial institution that has a licence (for example, another PSP). I suggest adding something like this:
** Telepass acknowledges and agrees that it assumes exclusive liability for the provision of Telepass Payment Service and proper operation of Telepass Payment Solutions. Telepass shall hold BOLT harmless from any claim or action in connection to the Telepass Payment Service and/or Telepass Payment Solutions resulting from the authorities or from the Customers themselves that is attributable to Telepass.
* clause 6.5 (a) - Telepass requested Bolt to provide T&Cs that incorporate Telepass Payment Solutions. We need to prepare a draft of these to discuss with Telepass.
* clause 6.6 (iii) - limitations to Telepass Payment Solutions - I understand that what they wanted to say is that Bolt should not impose additional limitations to Telepass Payment Solutions that are not imposed on other payment methods, i.e. that all payment methods offered by Bolt should be equal. Do we want to rephrase it (current wording seems clear to me)?
* clause 6.11 (c) - we need to send a final report vis telephone number. Do they mean fax? I think we need to remove "as well as to the Operations department via telephone number [06-97166620|tel:0697166620]", because it is their job to ensure proper communication within their own team.
* clauses 10.2, 10.5 and definition of "Location Data" - In these clauses Bolt is named as the owner of IPR and grants licence to use of IPR, but Bolt's entity that is the party to this agreement is not the owner of the relevant IPR and is not collecting the Location Data.
** I suggest amending definition of "Location Data" as follows: "refers to the set of real-time location data of the Motorcycles available for BOLT Rental, collected by BOLT *or its Affiliates*,...". We therefore need to add the definition of an "Affiliate" which shall be - “Affiliate” means, with respect to either party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with that party.
** I suggest amending clause 10.2 as follows: "...is the full and exclusive ownership of BOLT or its Affiliates and that,...".
** In terms of clause 10.5 BOLT is not owner of the Location Data and therefore cannot grant the licence to it.  We need to either add Bolt Ops as the party to this agreement in addition to Bolt Support IT or clarify whether granting such licence is within powers of Bolt Support IT as Location Data is not trademark and probably not governed by the intragroup IP agreement . Another point here is that this clause does not say that the licence is royalty free and specifically mentions that fee payable pursuant to section 8 contains the royalty - this may create a problem from the tax perspective (I had a similar problem with 3P Bolt Market agreements).
* clause 10.3 - We need to add this wording: "Telepass may use or reference BOLT's name, logo, trademarks or service marks in a press release or otherwise having acquired prior consent from BOLT and Telepass shall follow BOLT's Brand Guidelines available here: [https://bolt.eu/en/brand/guidelines/|https://bolt.eu/en/brand/guidelines/|smart-link] "
* section 11 - confidentiality clauses are very vague and also sharing of information with affiliates is not regulated (Bolt Ops will be a third party unless affiliates are exempt). Shall we add some standard clauses?
* section 12 - we need a review from the Privacy Team and advice on DPA and DSA.
* clause 17.1 (ii) - we need to add email address for notices.

Ok - so, internally speaking, our processes were not as advanced back then as they are now and currently we have 1) centralized these police requests and 2) created a process where we can effectively collaborate with the police while staying within the lines of the EU GDPR and other applicable data protection laws.

So, what happened in this case is: we asked the police to clarify the reason why they need the data (i.e. explain what the crime was) so that we can evaluate if we can disclose the data. They refused to do so → we refused to disclose the data.

What I advise to do in this case is to respond to them in this way:

{quote}At Bolt, we take the privacy and security of our customers, employees, and independent contractors very seriously. We only engage in data sharing with third parties where we are satisfied that the requirements of our third party data sharing policy have been met. This means that the request for data is lawful, necessary, proportionate, and limited to the specific purpose outlined in the request.

We have robust processes in place that help us both effectively collaborate with the police and stay within the lines of the EU GDPR and other applicable data protection laws. Namely, by providing the requested context, it will assist us in justifying providing the data you have requested.

Bolt is collaborating with the police and the format of the responses we provide has been sufficient to this day.

Again, Bolt would like to reiterate that always seek to assist law enforcement where we are able to. If you are able to assist us by pointing us towards the context we have requested, then we would be better placed to assist you.{quote}

Enterprises are obliged to provide copies of financial statements and consolidated financial statements at the request of legal entities and individuals in the manner prescribed by the Law of Ukraine "On Access to Public Information" and paragraph 8, part 3 of this article "The enterprise is obliged to ensure the availability of financial statements and consolidated financial statements for familiarization of legal entities and individuals according to their location."

Hi [~accountid:5ed4a25afbefc20c1d7d50da] and team

Here is the tax findings:

From a Swedish VAT perspective, the VAT treatments of transport of passengers are dependent on whether the transport partly are provided cross-border in another EU-country or solely in Sweden.

If the transport is made cross-border, then the transport is, as a whole, considered as provided outside of Sweden, even if the driver is registered in Sweden. In such case, no Swedish VAT should be added for transports of passengers if the transport partially are carried out in Denmark.

That means, for the rides from Sweden to Denmark (or from Denmark to Sweden), no VAT should be charged on the ride invoices.  Otherwise, the riders will be over-charged of VAT.  If the VAT is being charged and the riders are not private individuals, such input VAT is not creditable to them.

Do you know the number of cross border rides per month approximately?  The right way is to ask commerce team to distinguish cross-border rides from local rides and not to add VAT to the cross-border rides.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show/app the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report/or app indicators.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducted- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

The police authority's mission to fight crime is an important public interest. In order to be able to carry out this task, the authority is often dependent on receiving information held by private actors.
On May 25, 2018, the EU's data protection regulation began to apply in all member states. The Data Protection Ordinance applies as Swedish law and replaces the Personal Data Act (1998:204). Some general supplementary rules can be found in the law (2018:218) with supplementary provisions to the EU's data protection regulation, hereinafter referred to as the data protection law.
The police authority is responsible for its processing of personal data. This responsibility includes ensuring that the authority has legal support both for requesting personal data and for processing it once it has been received by the authority.
The police authority leads a preliminary investigation or assists the prosecutor during a preliminary investigation according to the regulations in ch. 23. the procedural code. During the preliminary investigation, evidence must be collected to investigate who can reasonably be suspected of the crime and whether there are sufficient grounds for prosecution. In order to be able to do this, the Police Authority often needs to access information held by other authorities and private actors. In the vast majority of cases, this is not a problem. If someone refuses to comply with the Police Authority, the authority can also, as a last resort, use criminal procedural coercive measures such as house searches and seizures.
The police authority has the right to process personal data for crime-fighting purposes with the support of the Crime Data Act (2018:1177) and the Police Data Act (2010:361). On 1 January 2019, the Police Data Act will be replaced by a new law on the police's processing of personal data within the scope of the Criminal Data Act.1 The regulations for the Police Authority's personal data processing in crime-fighting activities include both preliminary investigation and intelligence activities.
Information that is processed in preliminary investigations or intelligence operations is usually covered by confidentiality according to the provisions in ch. 18. 1 and 2 and 35 ch. §§ 1 of the Publicity and Confidentiality Act (2009:400), (OSL).
The police authority is responsible for personal data for its collection of personal data and the processing that subsequently takes place in the authority's operations. In a disclosure situation, the private actors must be able to trust that the Police Authority will only request information when there is a concrete and justified need for the information and legal prerequisites for processing by the authority.
When balancing interests, it should also be taken into account that the data is normally protected by the Police Authority through the confidentiality regulations in, among other things, 18 ch. 1 and 2 and 35 ch. §§ 1 OSL. In regards to your question on tendering, see below information on how the rental business operates: 

Rentals business operates three different business models:

* cross border (where Bolt Ops OU owns the fleet and offers the rental services)
* semi-localised (where the local entity owns the fleet and offers the rental services, Bolt Ops offers the App and collects payments)
* fully-localised (the local entity owns the fleet, offers the rental services, is contractually responsible for offering the Bolt App and collects it's own payments)

Ireland is currently operating an  e-bike fleet. So whichever business model is operating the e-bike business, it would follow the same for scooters

If Ireland is semi-localised and the local entity is the consumer facing "rental services provider" (also reflected in T&Cs) then it is the local entity that should apply for a tender and/or contract with local municipalities.

Hi [~accountid:61ae4180ebce470067c8cdc8]. In general to make a payment in EUR area you need to have *recipient name* and *bank account IBAN*. Most banks yet dont check if recipient name matches with IBAN, but if it is not clear to whom payment is sent then there is great chance that some party (or several) in the payment chain will stop the transaction for extra checks (AML, Sanctions compliance etc).

I am not sure why the full name is not presented on the bank card, but we should not add abbrevations/initials to the recipient name field. We should always enter full recipient name:

→ If it goes to a company, then only company name

→ If it goes to an individual, then only full individual name



This topic was also mentioned here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PFI-149674|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PFI-149674|smart-link]. Besides adding clear recipient name, adding *Date of Birth (DoB)* for individuals helps significantly to avoid delays in the payment processing. I can see that DoB have not been really added since the previous suggestion - Only 9 drivers in NL have DoB on their profile ([{color:#0747a6}+Example+{color}|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/3055237/?server=westeurope])

Of course. To provide a bit more context, we’ve created a manual redshift snapshot named {{do-not-delete-final-manual-snapshot-2024-01-04}}. Whenever Finance DWH team (Romet) needs to access the data in Redshift (1-2 times a year), Romet will re-create a redshift cluster from the manual redshift snapshot.

Because this is the only redshift snapshot we store, we want to protect it as much as possible from deletion and restrict only necessary Bolt employees to have access to it (for now, only Romet).

Internally, we’ve discussed all 3 alternative solutions:

* Option 1: we keep multiple manual snapshots, and we unload all commerce redshift tables onto s3 in the redshift aws account as another extra safety net.
* Option 2: we ingest these old redshift tables into {{dataeng}} aws account's presto.
* *Option 3*: we keep a manual snapshot “DO_NOT_DELETE_final_manual_snapshot_<creation_date>” and reduce access to the redshift aws account to max 3 people (Romet + 2 users from SRE team).

We concluded that *option 3 is more suitable option* and decided to proceed with it, in terms of the ops and maintenance complexity, safety and cost saving.

Let us know if you have any suggestions or if you need more information to proceed with option 3.

Thank you.

List of Injury and Damage Type

|*Injury Type*|*Description*|
|No injury|An event in which no one was harmed.|
|First Aid Injury|An event in which someone has gotten injured, but the injury is limited to bruising/scratches that can be treated by the person themselves with first aid.|
|Medical Treatment Injury|An event in which someone has gotten injured and required to be medically looked at by a professional (ambulance is called or the person is taken to the hospital).|
|Injury Impacting Lifestyle|Injury Impacting Lifestyle - an event in which someone has gotten injured and the injuries sustained will likely or have already caused them to miss work due to being "out of comission" while they recover.|
|Permanent Disability|An event in which someone has gotten injured and the injuries sustained have or will cause them to be permanently disabled.|
|Fatality|A event in which someone has gotten injured and the injuries sustained will result in their demise.|
|Unknown Injury|An event in which the injuries to the involved parties are unknown because the third party reporting it has not mentioned anything in reference to injuries.|
|*Damage Type*|*Description*|
|No Damage|An event in which nothing was damaged.|
|Superficial Damage|An event in which the damaged caused does not exceed superficial markings (e.g. scratches or the chipping of paint).|
|Parts Requiring Repair/Replacement|An event in which the damage requires repair, but has not compromised the structure of the object.|
|Structural Damage Requiring Repair|An event in which the damaged caused has impacted the structure of something to a moderate degree and will need to be repaired before further use.|
|Equipment Unusable|An event in which the damaged caused cannot be repaired.|
|Unknown Damage|An event in which the damaged caused cannot be determined as there is no reference to damages in the report.|

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *19/12/2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We share a copy of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order data on 2023-11-30 [Exported time: UTC]*

*As it also relates to a third party subject, a passenger, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice (ticket) received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending the penalty notice.*

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link] which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

hello [~accountid:616eb57ebcb5740068060e73],

*I have a couple of clarifications on the process in general:*
1. All driver’s account deletion requests should be handled only by the CS Team in all markets. We have a dedicated process described in Beehive that enhances our GDPR compliance. 

* Am I correct that in Czechia and Slovakia, it’s not the CS Team who works on the account deletion, but you + OPs?

2. In our privacy policies for drivers, we specify that after the account deletion we do store some financial data. Please note that according to the privacy law, we are entitled to keep some info, but only that info that is necessary for our purpose (legal obligation of Bolt to store ONLY financial info).

* It means that all account data should be deleted, except financial info we store.
* I appreciate that we do not delete all other info as we do not have yet the technical solution for this, but we should not disclose it publicly.

3. When the driver requests the account deletion and then ask for the re-activation, we should not re-activate the account as it discloses that we do not delete the data now as required under the GDPR.
4. We should prompt the driver to re-register with Bolt as a new driver.
5. We do have a driver’s re-activation process but only for BLOCKED drivers and only in the Driver Portal. 

* Reason: drivers need their financial info and we let them download it from the driver portal.

6. We currently do not re-activate accounts of deleted drivers even if they need their docs. In that case, they are entitled under the privacy law to make a request to us for receiving all the docs/info they need and we satisfy these requests within 1 month as prescribed by the GDPR.

*Summary:*
1. Please let me know which teams are responsible for account deletion and re-activation in these markets. If it’s not the CS, we have to set up a call and move all these tickets to the CS only.
2. The privacy team confirms that account re-activation is not allowed. Please do not re-activate the drivers. 

* If you receive these requests, please re-assign it to the CS or please follow this [Beehive instruction |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/44736]

3. If the driver is blocked and wants to re-activate the driver portal for getting some docs from there, please re-assign these requests to the CS Team that will follow the respective Beehive process.

So, to sum up my research and consultation with Cesar:

* we already collect and use IBANs in the vast majority of SEPA market (but remember that IBANs are 100% correct only in the finished payouts data)
* for Poland, we just need to take an existing account number and add {{PL}} - I can provide you with a query
* Sweden and UK are problematic for two reasons:
** IBAN includes two checksum digits that are calculated using [the MOD97 algorithm|https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1918217/the-mod97-operation-in-iban-validation] that is not so easy to implement - normally, to calculate it, [external tools|https://www.iban.com/iban-checker] are used, and we currently do not perform this check (but intend to do it as a part of validation tool in the future)
** In Sweden, the situation is even worse - the algorithm [depends on the bank|https://support.currencycloud.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360021346240-Bank-and-account-numbers-for-local-SEK-payments-], but we don’t collect this information
** In both markets, we make only *domestic payments*, where local bank details format is used, so we don’t collect, use, or store IBANs
* My proposal is to double check the documentation for DAC and make sure the IBAN is indeed requested everywhere - maybe there was a misunderstanding, because IBAN is not used for domestic payments in the UK and SE
* Even if the regulator requires it, Cesar advised that it may be cheaper not to comply to this request and pay a fine instead of implementing the IBAN check on our side. But I propose to discuss it with the regulator first.

[~accountid:5fc110f331795a006f947e12] the issue is, most of the time it is impossible to find the old courier and relocate the deposit. I have activated a ton of couriers who came from other countries with their own bags. This is why in all markets (Lithuania, Estonia, Croatia) this procedure is no longer active for a long time.

If the deposit is added once and will be returned - great, I see no issue here. If the deposit is relocated and returned from/for the old account - again, great, no issues here. One deposit was paid and one was returned. 

My concern comes from the new couriers that come with a Bolt bag. We will not be able to return 2 deposits to the courier, only 1 will be returned, meaning, the courier gets overcharged. Again, this procedure is used only in Latvia, cops,  LV TL’s and quality teams from other countries agree that charging 2 times (courier paid for the bag and a deposit was added as well) if only 1 is returned - concerning.

So answering the question “Could you please elaborate on how the +*new courier*+ is charged twice here?” - courier paid for the bag (one payment) and was charged a deposit (second payment). After returning this bag courier would get only 1 payment back. The second one is never paid back. This is an overcharge.

*SUMMARY of Risks connected with giving benefits to drivers (minimum wage, holiday pay, and pensions)*

Bolt’s ability to defend against reclassification proceedings depends on its ability, mainly, to demonstrate the absence of a requirement for personal service.

The provision of minimum wage, holiday pay, and pension arrangements could be a factor supporting an employee or worker relationship.

In determining the case, the courts will assess the overall relationship between the client and the contractor. 
The UK case law suggests that these benefits are customary in worker or employee relationships and atypical arrangements between a client and a professional business this could suggest that there is a worker or employee-like arrangement.
Therefore, what it suggests is that there is a risk of increasing reclassification risks by introducing these “employment benefits”.

*Minimum wage and holiday pay -* This risk is higher, especially in the case of offering minimum wage, and holiday pay benefits.

Furthermore, the standard regulation stipulates that employees should have the opportunity to use their holidays, and only if they are unable to do so, the employer must compensate them for the unused holidays. If Bolt diverges from this standard rule, it diminishes the risk of the benefit being labeled as employment benefits, however, the question is whether such payment would be considered as holiday pay at all and whether would Bolt be able to offset those payments in case of reclassification.

*Pensions* - In terms of pensions, the risk is somewhat reduced due to Bolt's planned model for pension benefits. Bolt intends to provide these benefits on an opt-in basis, differing from the legally mandated approach where employees are automatically enrolled and can opt-out.

Hi Carlos,

Sure, basically, all SEPA EUR countries have switched to using international IBAN format: 

AT, BE, CY, DE, EE, ES, FI, FR, HR, IE, IT, LT, LV, MT, NL, PT, SI, SK - IBAN

Non-EUR countries use IBAN for cross-border payments and local format for domestic payments. However, in the majority of these markers we also collect and store IBANs, which the bank transforms into the local account format ([example|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/invoicing-payment/payouts/view/147702433]):

CZ, HU, NO, PL, RO - IBAN

(as I mentioned, in PL we may also collect local numbers, but it’s not a problem).

One exception is Sweden. We use local format (it does not have any special name) that consists of bank account number (up to 12 digits) + routing code (up to 5 digits). In some [sources|https://www.atlar.com/guides/bank-payments-in-sweden], you will also see 3-digit bank codes. 

Account number + bank code + 6 check digits give BBAN (Basic Bank Account Number) format which seems to be used by the bank. But we don’t collect the bank details in BBAN format, it is derived by the bank from the local format.

Here is how it looks like in the payout request xml file: 

Account number: 0169540

Routing code: 3075

<Nm>Tomas Abraham</Nm>
</Cdtr>

Journal of Laws

h3. Journal of Laws 2023.2119, i.e

Act in force

Version from: October 3, 2023 to: April 17, 2026

Art. 96.  [Admission to drive a vehicle contrary to the requirements]

§ 1. 

The owner, holder, user or driver of a vehicle who, on a public road, in a residential zone or traffic zone, allows:

to drive a vehicle a person who does not have the physical or mental fitness to drive a vehicle properly,

a person who does not have the required license to drive a vehicle,

a person under the influence of alcohol or a similarly acting substance to drive a vehicle,

a vehicle for driving despite the lack of the required documents confirming the vehicle's admission to traffic,

a vehicle for driving, even though the vehicle is not properly equipped with the required devices and instruments or even though they are unsuitable for their intended purpose,

to use a motor vehicle in a manner inconsistent with its intended purpose,

is punishable by a fine.

§ 2. 

The same penalty for the acts specified in § 1 points 1, 3-6 and for unintentionally allowing a person to drive a vehicle on a public road without the required authorization shall be subject to the vehicle dispatcher or the person whose duties include his/her activities, and if such a person has not been appointed - manager of the unit that owns the vehicle.

§ 3. 

The same penalty shall be imposed on anyone who, contrary to his/her obligation, fails to indicate, at the request of an authorized body, to whom he or she has entrusted the vehicle to drive or use it at a specified time.
