Hi [~accountid:639212cda593cb822e99192b]  - thanks for raising this.

In summary, this isn’t the sort of campaign we’d ideally run, I’m afraid. 

By offering ‘compensation’ or a ‘promise’ for a failed scheduled ride it’s very much making out that we (Bolt) are responsible for these journeys when it’s legally essential that we’re not responsible at all. 

For background, most of our T+Cs very specifically say *_'we aren't providing you with transport services and we don't promise you anything'_*. Anything we put in our comms / campaigns will take priority over our T+Cs, so we need to be careful.

For these reasons, any campaign that’s offering any form of gesture for a failed journey as a ‘bonus’ must also make it clear that Bolt is not responsible for the journeys. Yet in doing that, I appreciate that it would cut across the commercial reason for the campaign - so that’s not ideal either.

{color:#ff991f}Ultimately, it’s much better to promote the ability to book a scheduled ride {color}{color:#ff991f}_without_{color}{color:#ff991f} this sort of promise - so that is the leading recommendation from the legal side (unfortunately).{color}

However, if it’s commercially essential that you need to promote on this basis, there is scope to take a commercial view and run this campaign. In which case:

* you should definitely drop the phrases ‘promise a driver', ‘our commitment’ and ‘compensation’ because that _does_ potentially set us up for claims for the cost of missed flights etc. Anything which will lure a customer into using the service on the basis that it’s ‘reliable’ will be a contractual promise that it is.
* the messaging  must avoid sounding like we ‘own / control / are responsible for’ drivers. You'll probably be familiar with these ‘reclassification’ issues but if not have a [quick look at this page|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONTENT/pages/4468998200/Reclassification+Risk+Copy+Guide] <- this applies to all campaigns. The copy team, who must review all comms messages before they go out externally, will scan for these issues but it’s important that what you give them has been revised by you first as they are not solely responsible for spotting these issues.
* we should make it clear that Bolt cannot guarantee the journey, because the services are provided by independent drivers / fleet companies. This is also very important to help reduce the reclassification concerns. This is dealt with by the wording in red below.

One approach might be to just keep these gesture as a minor comment rather than lead with it in promo material:

_”Scheduled rides - hooray!_

…

{color:#ff5630}_Please note that as transportation services are provided by third party independent drivers and fleet companies, Bolt cannot guarantee that any scheduled ride will take place_{color}_, but in these circumstances Bolt will provide you with a discount voucher for [X] to be used for future journeys as a gesture of good will.“ etc._

You and the copy team would need to play around with this wording to provide ‘consumer friendly wording’ that balances out addressing these concerns whilst meeting your commercial objectives.

I hope that helps - I will now close this ticket but do please reach out if you need further input. 

Thanks.

_A side note: in principal model markets (only the UK at present) Bolt DOES provide the transportation services, so there is more of a scope to make these sorts of promises. However, we still run into the issue of making ourselves ‘more liable' for failed journeys… any attempt to run this in the UK should be raised specifically with the UK ops and legal teams for review._

Dear Ms Zanevskaya,

We are writing to you in response to your request through the European Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform with reference number 2023/DT138666. 

We appreciate your claim and the proposed solutions. In this regard, we would like to make the following clarifications and hopefully provide you with further details on how the Bolt platform is already addressing the solutions envisaged.

* *full documentation package for all drivers (there are many stories in Portugal of drivers driving without being registered in the system)*

All TVDE drivers in Portugal need to fulfil the requirements established by Law n.o 45/2018 de 10 de agosto. In particular, every driver needs to hold a driving license for at least 3 years, a certificate of TVDE driver issued by the national authority, a course certificate to become a TVDE driver issued by a third party and no criminal record. 

In compliance with the current legislation, Bolt requires these documents for all drivers in the platform, which are verified at the moment a driver account is activated and later on at the time of expiry/renewal of such documents.

Due to privacy related principles, we are unfortunately not able to share this personal data with passengers and make available the documentation for each driver.

* *Control of cars so that there is no extra hours (there are stories of two or three drivers driving one car so that the car is not idle, but only one driver is registered in the system)*

The profession of TVDE drivers is regulated in Portugal. Consequently, only drivers with an account in the platform and fulfilling the legal requirements are able to legally provide transportation services. 

In addition to the documentation compliance in place, we have recently introduced an identity verification tool to ensure only registered drivers provide transportation services through our platform. This means that drivers in the Bolt platform are required to submit a real-time selfie as part of our identity verification process not only as part of the registration process but also later on on a regular basis.

Passengers are also important partners in maintaining the safety of the platform. We recommend each passenger to check that the driver’s face, car make and registration plate match those shown in the app. When in doubt passengers can send us reports that prompt us to to double check the concerns raised.

* *Audio or video monitoring in the car during trips, for the safety of both passenger and driver*

Even though we are committed with the highest safety standard, we must ensure any such measures are implemented in accordance with local regulations. Many markets do not enable electronic platforms to implement audio or video monitoring features, however we have recently introduced a safety feature that allow passengers to share trip details. This allows passengers to send the car's make, model, registration number, and live location to friends or family via a shareable link.

* *Instruction to drivers on what they can and cannot do*

Following local regulations, TVDE drivers in electronic platforms work at the service of certified TVDE operators in Portugal. These TVDE operators are independent companies from Bolt and the drivers at their service therefore autonomous from Bolt. 

Nevertheless, the profession of TVDE driver is regulated in Portugal and therefore TVDE operators and their drivers compelled to provide their services in compliance with legislation in place.

* *New phone or cash compensation*

In accordance with article 15(2) of the Passenger’s terms and conditions available for consultation on our website, “_the Service and Application are provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis. This means that Bolt does not represent, warrant or guarantee that Your use of the Service and Your access to the Application will be uninterrupted, without delay, error free or will meet Your expectations and Bolt makes no commitment in relation to the performance or availability of the Service in these Terms of Service and, to the extent possible, excludes any commitments which may be provided by law._” Consequently, following article 15(3) of the same terms and conditions, “_Bolt accepts no liability for any claim arising from the provision of the Service._”

{quote}The current set-up of the billing system allows to create billing records for adjustments and compensations for past periods. This leads to incomplete cost and revenue recognition and / or cut-off errors in Workday. 

Billing records created by the billing system include two different date fields:
Action timestamp: Defines the time of the corresponding action (price review finished, order finished, refund requested, etc.).
Creation date: Date of billing record creation.
The period of revenue and cost recognition in Workday is based on the action timestamp of billing records. However, only billing records with creation date before the monthly closing activities for revenue and receivables are recognised. The cut-off date is the 3rd-5th working day. Billing records created after the cut-off date for previous periods are not automatically moved to the FDWH data models and therefore not recognised in financial reporting. 

An analysis for the period of January - October 2023 performed by the FDWH team revealed there were billing records with a total cost value of 319k € created for driver and fleet compensations / adjustments with creation date later than 5 days after monthly closing. This is how the task went for me starting 2nd January - written down mostly based on Git commits: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86371/commits|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86371/commits|smart-link]  and slack threads.

# Started from PR that Agustin has published on Tuesday 2th January, based on base PR from previous reissue provided by Vishal.

h3. Trying to create the table with Alter Automation

# The PR assumes creating a new table, and the Alter Automation system noticed this and encouraged creating it using Alter Automation process.
# The Alter Automation PR had Linter Errors related to DB Schema. The errors were related to Encoding - they were a false positive, but ultimately to make it happy, we’ve made these two changes:
## [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/510b5cc33fa5a3d5f7458df3072531cd67c68ee3|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/510b5cc33fa5a3d5f7458df3072531cd67c68ee3|smart-link]
## [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/225c8b5551cf16d87308ee3ddf5daf8e8d9abba5|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/225c8b5551cf16d87308ee3ddf5daf8e8d9abba5|smart-link]
# Alter Automation wasn’t updating the PR, so we’ve created a new PR every time - that’s why there’s so many branches attached to this JIRA. Waiting for the Alter Automation linter also took time.
# The Alter Automation ultimately didn’t work anyway, because it had an ongoing bug during the time - see: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CN6SFK4SW/p1704285113682789|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CN6SFK4SW/p1704285113682789|smart-link]  and we’ve ended up creating the table the old way, by request to Service Desk.

Waiting for Alter Automation PR updates took time due to delays. It also took time to realize I need to recreate a PR.

h3. Testing on PRELIVE Part 1

# In order to test on PRELIVE, we’ve found some orders on PRELIVE, and updated the CSV to use them.
# There was an issue with PRELIVE. Nothing looked wrong so the first thought was that it was the end-of-line problem, so I’ve removed an end-of-line symbol.
# it was actually a column name error {{invoice_sub_type -> invoice_subtype}}. After this, the parse step worked.
# Test on PRELIVE showed that the External ID API changed. Thread: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03FY31JC7L/p1704354454143099|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03FY31JC7L/p1704354454143099|smart-link]  Commit solving:  [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/ff747f6e7950d37e1180129da2d192725efb422e|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/ff747f6e7950d37e1180129da2d192725efb422e|smart-link]  The client now needed to provide a different {{invoice_external_id}} in the reissued invoice, which wasn’t the case before.
## *Basically, the code we’ve copy-pasted from old branch was understandably outdated. This could have been avoided if instead of copy-pasting, we’ve kept it in the repo.*
# Another issue with copy-pasted code was that the migration state wasn’t being updated, so we’ve fixed this as well. It was probably never needed, *due to previous use-case being simpler*.

All of steps above took time waiting on deploying to PRELIVE - that takes about 3-5 minutes, so not as bad as waiting for DB pull-request or LIVE.

h3. Updating to the new requirements

After showing results on PRELIVE, we’ve realized missed requirements: in addition to simply reissuing the invoice, we also need to update the VAT, and Invoice Issuer data.

*After implementing that:*

# We’ve realized there are also REFUND cases, and SUBSCRIPTION cases in the file, so I’ve found some orders in PRELIVE, added them to the PRELIVE CSV file.
# *Invoice Inactive error* - it turns out that reissuing a Refund causes error that says that the invoice is inactive. We’ve made a change to *skip such rows* and *mark them as IGNORE in the db*.
## [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/7e6f2a7a1f8786b33877f8ddf2088575980bdce9|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/86090/commits/7e6f2a7a1f8786b33877f8ddf2088575980bdce9|smart-link] 
## [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03FY31JC7L/p1704368991983569|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03FY31JC7L/p1704368991983569|smart-link] 
# After that, the *PRELIVE* worked.

The iteration here was also a PRELIVE deployment, so ~5 minutes and a lot of clicking.

h3. Trying in LIVE

# Due to prior issues, we’ve first tested on a mini LIVE dataset with 6 rows. *Then we’ve started with the “big” full dataset of 70k rows.*
# The “big” dataset was going slow, 300 rows per minute. This meant about 4 hours of work. I’ve tweaked a configuration and restarted a cron.
# Due to restart, however, the cron couldn’t start-up, because it tried to reissue an invoice that was already reissued. Basically the cron wasn’t idempotent. I’ve added a last commit, a code to ignore “invoice already exists” error.
# Tweaking with configuration didn’t help - *it seems 500 per minute (of getDocument & reissueDocument pair of queries) is Billing Document’s limit*.

LIVE deployment takes 20-30 minutes, so iterations here were pretty slow to deploy.

h3. Finally

After the proces has finished (after about 2 hours) we’ve reverted the deployment (the code wasn’t merged to develop).

h3. Final thoughts

* In retrospect, overwriting Invoice Issuer on the document wasn’t ultimately needed, because it was practically identical (cosmetic change only). Hardcoding VAT rate would be sufficient. But that wasn’t a source of many problems anyway.
* In the future, if we copy-paste, we should keep error handling / skipping failed rows in the logic from the get go, otherwise it’s hard to iterate.
* LIVE deployment takes 20-30 minutes, so we should avoid keeping CSV in the repo.
* The process can be improved, see next comment.

h3. A better process idea

*Part 1: Provide reissued invoice IDs to the system* - instead of using CSV, insert them into the table from local environment. Many bugs documented in my previous comment will be avoided, and iteration process will be faster, especially in LIVE.

*Part 2: Storing a reissue invoice data in the db* - instead of using a custom table, use *the task framework* - add a new TaskRowType, and use a Task framework to execute. This will avoid the state management code, the table adding problems documented in my previous comment, and so on. I have gathered all the applicable VAT form changes, as per below:

* Line 1 of VAT return:

Acts and transactions subject to tax at a rate of 22% (line 1 of VAT return (KMD))

* line 1'1 of VAT return:

Acts and transactions subject to tax at a rate of 20% (line 1 of VAT return (KMD) until the taxation period of 12.2023, line 1'1 started from the taxation period of 01.2024)

* Line 4 of VAT return:

Total amount of value-added tax (22% of line 1 +20% of line 1'1 + 9 % of line 2) from the taxation period of 01.2024

* Line 5 of VAT return:

Includes 22% VAT from the taxation period of 01.2024

* Lines 5.1 - 5.4 of VAT return:

Includes 22% VAT from the taxation period of 01.2024.



Please notice that our preference is to have a new VAT declaration report applicable since 2024 with necessary box amendments and leave the current declaration as it is (for historical reasons).

Hi [~accountid:62d01789bd54f8d3ffb6c03d] , 

As discussed during our call on Friday last week, the City of Gothenburg is an authority that has the right to issue permits for certain business activities such as the rental of scooters and e-bikes. The terms of the permit from the City of Gothenburg govern the pricing, any other commercial terms and requirements as well as the possibility to terminate. 

The police permit is simply a permit to use public spaces for the business activities (parking zones). The police permit is based on the terms governed in the City permit, in other words, the police permit does not affect the price or the right to terminate (as this is governed in the City permit). 

*Therefore, the relevant permit in order to amend any terms or terminate the permit is the City permit.* 

The City permit from last year does not include any termination rights or any rights to amend the number of scooters. Since we have not seen what the permit looks like in this round or the application form we can’t review or assess the terms of this City permit. 

*Next steps*

* As the permits have not been issued yet and the City in an email provided the option to change the numbers for certain months without providing a specific deadline, we recommend to involve Public Policy in order to find an amicable solution with the city. The lack of a specified deadline may be used as an argument in such discussions. 
* The City has a responsibility to inform you of your rights to challenge the city’s decision. If the City refuses to amend the numbers, we recommend requesting that the City informs you of your rights under the permit and applicable laws. 
* If the permit is issued without changes to the numbers and you wish to take legal action, please forward the permit documentation to us in the Legal Team. We can then review the document and relevant local laws to determine if there are any actions we can take. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

After getting help from my colleagues and reasoning more about the logs we came up with the follow scenario about what happened:

# We see multiple reverse_geocode calls because the user moved the pin on the map(from checkout screen). We cannot confirm this because the reverse geocode calls from the logs don’t have 10 decimals as we were expecting. A reason for this might be because that table is an old one and the coordinates are trimmed to fewer decimals.
# 2 calls that had predicted entrance(33 , 31B in this order) got written in the metadata cache using the same key so actually the details for address 31B was stored there. Here is the actual bug.
# The user opened the map one more time and without moving the pin he confirmed the location ⇒ we have a recordLocationEntered where the coordinates have just a few decimals but the address string is from the initial getDeliveryLocation(with 33). On the backend, we used the received coordinates to get the place details from the Metadata cache and we actually got the details(the place id) for 31B

I’ve tested locally the following scenario, using local debezium + mysql + kafka docker-compose setup.

* Stop Kafka Connect worker docker container, send {{null}} tombstone to the same partition in the “offset” topic, insert 2 rows into a MySQL table, start Kafka Connect worker docker container again. 

I’ve observed that the Kafka Connect worker container started successfully, the 2 records didn’t get send to Kafka, inserting another row in the MySQL table sends a record to Kafka. Essentially, the 2 rows are missed and Debezium starts reading from the current binlog because the binlog offset stored in the “offset” topic is {{null}}.



Notes:

To prove that restarting Kafka Connect worker container doesn’t affect it from picking up the binlog offset from the “offset” topic, I’ve also done tests of the 2 following scenarios:

* Restart Connect Worker container: restart is successful, inserting 1 new row after Connect Worker Restart also sends 1 record to Kafka
* Stop Connect Worker container, insert 2 rows into MySQL, start Connect Worker: Connect Worker restarted successfully, 2 records are automatically sent to Kafka after Connect Worker restarts
